{{Imperial Household Rituals}}

'''Imperial Household Ritual Ordinance''' (皇室祭祀令, Kōshitsu Saishi Rei) was a {{ill|Law|ja|法令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Law|1=regulations|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106947327}} concerning {{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rituals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭|1=Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q132241}} of the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial Household|1=Imperial House of Japan}}. It was promulgated as {{ill|Imperial Household Ordinance|ja|皇室令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Ordinance|1=Imperial Household Ordinance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11581032}} No. 1 in 1908 during the Meiji period and abolished on May 2, 1947, by {{ill|Imperial Household Ordinance No. 12 of 1947|ja|皇室令及附屬法令廢止ノ件|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Ordinance No. 12 of 1947|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Despite its abolition, {{ill|Ritual ceremonies of the Imperial Palace|en|Ritual ceremonies of the Imperial Palace|qid=Q11453226|lt=Ceremonies of the Japanese Imperial Palace|1=Ritual ceremonies of the Imperial Palace}} continue to follow the provisions of the Imperial Household Ritual Ordinance.

== Overview ==

The ordinance consisted of three chapters: Chapter 1 (General Provisions), Chapter 2 (Great Rites), and Chapter 3 (Minor Rites).

The ritual format was outlined in the appendix of the ordinance, with Part 1 covering Great Rite Formats and Part 2 covering Minor Rite Formats.

Article 10 stipulated ceremonial anniversaries ({{ill|Shikinen-sai|ja|式年祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinen-sai|qq=}}) at intervals of 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100 years, and every 100 years thereafter following a sovereign's {{ill|Demise of the Crown|en|Demise of the Crown|qid=Q842994|lt=Imperial Demise|1=Demise of the Crown}}. Other provisions included rituals during mourning periods (Articles 4 and 5), practices related to purification (Article 6), and rites involving tombs, official shrines, and other facilities (Articles 7, 23). Specific distinctions were also made regarding rituals held at the {{ill|Kashiko-dokoro|ja|賢所|1=Kashiko-dokoro|2=ja|3=賢所|4=fr|5=Kashiko-dokoro|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiko-dokoro|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiko-dokoro|qq=}}, {{ill|Kōrei-den|ja|皇霊殿|lt=Kōrei-den (Imperial Ancestral Shrines)|1=Three Palace Sanctuaries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōrei-den|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Palace Sanctuaries|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宮中三殿}}, {{ill|Shinden|ja|八神殿|1=Hasshinden|1=Hasshinden|lt=Shinden|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinden|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasshinden|qq=}} ([[Three Palace Sanctuaries]]), and other sites (Articles 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 23, 24, 25).

=== Great Rites ===

Great Rites ({{ill|大祭|ja|大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/大祭|1=Grand Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11438341}}) were performed personally by the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|qid=Q208233|lt=Emperor|1=Emperor of Japan}}, accompanied by the {{ill|Imperial Family|ja|皇族|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Family|1=Imperial Family of Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11581068}} and {{ill|Bureaucrat|en|Bureaucrat|qid=Q572700|lt=Officials|1=Bureaucrat}}, or were conducted in a similar manner. They involved three days of purification, the wearing of ceremonial attire, and the presentation of the sacred imperial regalia during appearances.

* {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}} - January 3
* {{ill|Kigensetsu Festival|ja|紀元節祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigensetsu Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} - February 11
* {{ill|Spring Koryosai|ja|春季皇霊祭|1=Kōreisai|lt=Spring Kōreisai|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spring Koryosai|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōreisai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 皇霊祭}} - Vernal Equinox
* Spring Shrine Festival - Vernal Equinox
* {{ill|Emperor Jimmu Festival|ja|神武天皇祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmu Emperor Festival|qq=}} - April 3
* {{ill|Autumn Koryosai|ja|秋季皇霊祭|1=Kōreisai|lt=Autumn Kōreisai|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Autumn Koryosai|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōreisai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 皇霊祭}} - Autumnal Equinox
* Autumn Shrine Festival - Autumnal Equinox
* {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}} - October 17
* {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}} - November 23–24
* {{ill|Previous Emperor Festival|ja|先帝祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Previous Emperor Festival|qq=}} - Anniversary of previous emperors' deaths
* Decennial Rites for the three preceding sovereigns - Anniversaries of their passing
* Decennial Rites for previous empresses - Anniversaries of their passing
* Decennial Rites for imperial consorts - Anniversaries of their passing

Additionally, Great Rites were held for significant imperial or national occasions, including announcements to the {{ill|List of Jingū|en|List of Jingū|qid=Q120680118|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=List of Jingū}}, construction-related rituals, and the enshrinement or relocation of imperial spirits.

=== Minor Rites ===

Minor Rites ({{ill|小祭|ja|小祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/小祭|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) were led by the {{ill|Shōtenchō|ja|掌典長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōtenchō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 掌典職|1=Chief Cleric of the Imperial Household|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498167}} or conducted similarly, with the Emperor performing worship alongside the Imperial Family and officials. These rites involved purification, ceremonial attire, and presentation of sacred regalia during appearances.

* {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} - January 1
* {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai|1=Kinensai}} - February 17
* Kashiko-dokoro Mikagura - Mid-December
* {{ill|Tenchōsetsu Festival|ja|天長節祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchōsetsu Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} - Emperor's Birthday
* Annual Rites for the three preceding sovereigns - Anniversaries of their passing
* Annual Rites for preceding empresses - Anniversaries of their passing
* Annual Rites for imperial consorts - Anniversaries of their passing
* Decennial Rites for the sovereigns from Emperor Suizei onward - Anniversaries of their passing

Other Minor Rites included rituals for enshrining spirits of consorts, crown princes, and other members of the Imperial Family into the {{ill|Kōrei-den|ja|皇霊殿|lt=Kōrei-den (Imperial Ancestral Shrines)|1=Three Palace Sanctuaries|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōrei-den|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Palace Sanctuaries|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宮中三殿}}.
